title: C482/2131/2023 of HIMANSHU CHAUDHARY Vs GIRISH CHANDRA CHAUDHARY

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
C482 No2131 of 2023
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Sagar Kothari, learned counsel for the
applicant.
In the instant C482 Application, the
applicant has put a challenge to the
proceedings of Complaint Case No.3160 of
2023, "Girish Chaudhary Vs. Himanshu
Chaudhary", in which the present applicant has
been summoned by an order of 25.09.2023 for
being tried for the offences under Sections 447
and 427 of the IPC.
There are two fold arguments of the
learned counsel for the applicant. He contends
that on a simplicitor reading of the complaint as
instituted by the respondent on 18.04.2023
before the Court of Additional Judicial
Magistrate, Dehradun, no apparent offence of
mischief falling under Section 425 of the IPC
could be made out, for the purpose to attract an
offence under Section 427 of the IPC.
Secondly, he argues that the registration of
the complaint case is counterblast to the
proceedings under Order 39 Rule 2A of the CPC
as it was drawn by him in Misc. Case No.40 of
2023, "Himanshu Chaudhary Vs. Girish

Chaudhary and Others", which was emanating
from Original Suit No.912 of 2020.
This Court feels it apt to deal with the
second argument first, before answering the
first argument, as to whether it is a mischief
under Section 425 of the IPC or not.
The issue of counterblast could be only
when the principal proceedings is being taken
as to be an impediment, but here the
proceedings under Order 39 Rule 2A of the
CPC, is a misc. proceedings of violation of
temporary injunction under Order 39 Rule 1
and 2 of the CPC as granted on 24.12.2021.
A misc. proceeding should not be confused
with the principal proceedings of Suit No.40 of
2023. Besides that, the institution of
proceedings under Order 39 Rule 2A of the CPC
for violation of the interim injunction dated
24.12.2021, is only a penal in nature, the issue
which is to be decided by the learned Civil
Court which is seized with the proceedings of
under Order 39 Rule 2A of the CPC.
May be institution of the proceedings of a
Misc. Case under Order 39 Rule 2A of the CPC
will not grant an immunity to the applicant that
for his criminal act, no complaint could be
registered against him.
Hence, registration of a subsequent
complaint on 18.04.2023, would not be a

counterblast, for the reason being, that in case
if the allegations levelled in the complaint itself
is taken into consideration, particularly, as
referred to in paragraph no.2, 3 of the
complaint, whether the actual complaint was to
the effect that the complainant had broken the
lock of the shop and the house and had
damaged the same on 04.04.2023.
Issue would be as to whether the act of
complainant of the incident of 04.04.2023
would be a mischief under Section 425 of the
IPC itself or not.
Section 425 of the IPC reads as under:-
"Whoever with intent to cause, or
knowing that he is likely to cause, wrongful
loss or damage to the public or to any
person, causes the destruction of any
property, or any such change in any property
or in the situation thereof as destroys or
diminishes its value or utility, or affects it
injuriously, commits "mischief".
That to constitute an act of mischief, there
has to be an intent to, with knowledge to cause
damage or loss.
Paragraph no.2 speaks about the action
taken on 04.04.2023 where the allegation are
about barging into the shop and the residence
by breaking the lock and the shutters. Whether
actually the incident of mischief as complained
of in paragraph no.2 has chanced or not, is a
subject which has to be decided by the trial

Court, but the action complained in paragraph
no.2 to be read with contents of paragraph no.3
of the complaint would be a mischief, because it
has resulted into causing of a damage by the
untoward act of the applicant, which was
complained of by filing an application under
Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C.
For the reasons aforesaid, I am not
inclined to interfere in the C482 Application
and the same would, accordingly, stand
dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 01.11.2023
Sukhbant
